name: Study Permit

application_window.note: 2026 cap: maximum 309,670 study-permit applications accepted for processing, gated by a Provincial/Territorial Attestation Letter (PAL/TAL); IRCC targets issuing up to ~408,000 permits total (155,000 new arrivals, 253,000 extensions)

requirements.blocker_text: This requires acceptance from a Designated Learning Institution (DLI) and — for most applicants — a Provincial/Territorial Attestation Letter (PAL/TAL), part of the 2024-introduced cap system.
requirements.fix_path: Secure DLI acceptance and the required PAL/TAL.

value.note: single applicant, outside Quebec; Quebec uses a separate figure of $24,617 CAD; indexed annually to LICO

requirements.blocker_text: This requires proof of funds of at least $22,895 CAD (single applicant, outside Quebec), on top of first-year tuition and travel costs.

evidence_required.document: Letter of acceptance from a DLI
Proof of funds meeting the required threshold

outcome.duration_length: duration of the study program, renewable

notes: FORMULA VALUE, tier-1 confirmed: $22,895 CAD effective since 1 Sept 2025, a $2,260 rise from the $20,635 set 1 Jan 2024 (itself up sharply from a long-frozen $10,000) — indexed annually to LICO (Low Income Cut-Off). Quebec uses a separate figure ($24,617 CAD, effective 1 Jan 2026). GENUINE 2024-era STRUCTURAL CHANGE still shaping 2026: the PAL/TAL cap system introduced in 2024 caused study-permit holders to fall from over 1 million (Jan 2024) to roughly 725,000 (Sept 2025) — a dramatic, confirmed contraction. NEW EXEMPTION from 1 Jan 2026: master's and doctoral students at PUBLIC DLIs no longer need a PAL/TAL — also exempt: K-12 students, the FMCSP pilot, exchange/scholarship holders, and same-DLI/same-level extensions. Direct feeder into ca_pgwp, closing Canada's version of the core Journey chain seen throughout this dataset.
